Properties on Roberta's residential edges back directly to rural-acreage source habitat. The combination produces consistent dispersal pressure year-round. Across Roberta, the tricolored bat (Perimyotis subflavus, now ESA-listed) is documented in middle Georgia and may roost in pre-1900 Main Street chimney colonies. Pre-1900 Roberta chimney colonies may include tricolored individuals — exclusion timing must comply with federal ESA protocols. Roberta bat-exclusion windows on pre-1900 chimney colonies run September through early November and March through mid-May. The May-August maternity window is closed under Georgia DNR rules. For Roberta pre-1900 chimney-roost properties, the November-March winter torpor window is closed under federal tricolored bat ESA protocols.

Roberta pre-1900 chimney bat exclusion follows the one-way valve protocol — install valves at active brick-mortar entry points, monitor emergence over 7-14 days, remove valves once the colony fully evacuates, seal permanently with mortar matching the original.
